correctness.rationale: For \(n\ge2\) and every finite field, \(\operatorname{GL}_n\) is transitive on nonzero vectors and ordered independent pairs. Distinct proportional targets cannot both be idempotents. Independent targets with dependent squared source vectors also cannot both occur. The joint probability for the remaining pairs is \(1/((q^n-1)(q^n-q))\). Coordinatewise squaring in characteristic two is a semilinear bijection and preserves linear dependence. In odd characteristic, a support-\(r\) vector admits exactly \((q-1)(2^{r-1}-1)\) independent partner vectors with proportional squares. Summing over supports gives the stated exceptional count, so the mean equals one and the variance equals the second factorial moment. Positivity for dimension at least two and elementary leading-term estimates verify all boundaries and asymptotics. Ten complete finite-field matrix tests, with separate exceptional-pair enumeration for small field-vector spaces, reproduce the formula but do not replace its proof.

originality.rationale: The accessible 37-page 2026 survey explicitly supplies the unit mean (Remark 23, p. 19), asks about random evolution algebras (Question 22, p. 23), and proposes an unproved fixed-point distribution (Conjecture 2, p. 27), but states no exact variance or second factorial moment. Wei and Zou enumerate isomorphism-class orbits, a different invariant and measure. An existing complete dimension two distribution implies only that specialization; the new n-uniform formula, especially all dimension at least three, is not implied by it. Index and web searches for variance, paired idempotents, second moments and dependency of coordinatewise squares returned no covering claim. Priority remains qualified by possible implicit older coverage.

value.rationale: Remark 23 of arxiv:2610.22248v1 motivates finite-field idempotent statistics by proving only the universal mean, while Conjecture 2 makes stronger probabilistic predictions. The new exact variance for every dimension is the first fluctuation invariant beyond that mean; it explains why odd fields have a strict finite-field correction and characteristic two has unit variance at every dimension at least two. The proof identifies an explicit support-and-sign obstruction and establishes convergence of the second factorial moment without assuming the unproved full-distribution conjecture. This is not a reformulation of the mean or a restatement of existing two-dimensional enumerations: the structural formula applies to every higher dimension.
